feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level progression, credible scope, and a consistent focus on digital communications strategy. It reads professionally and is well aligned to communications leadership roles, though it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer repeated ideas, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms and tools: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Clarity, Airtable, etc.  
- Writing is polished and generally concise, with good emphasis on strategy, governance, workflows, and mission-driven communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but fewer show outcomes such as growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “content operations and enterprise web improvement” could use a comma); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” and reduce stacked nouns like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs.”
- Add sharper positioning tied to recent roles: emphasize enterprise web strategy, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, and governance for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad claims like “Expert in” with more concrete leadership language such as “Leads” or “Specializes in.”
- Possible rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improves coordination across complex teams. Brings deep experience in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, audience-focused content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Platform modernization” overlaps with Topline Skills and NACo experience; keep the intro high-level rather than listing tools or platforms.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, CV-aligned phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS modernization & administration,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Analytics, insights & performance reporting.”
- Prioritize strategic and recent strengths first: Digital strategy & transformation • Web platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Cross-channel communications leadership.
- Reduce softer phrasing like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” to “Stakeholder alignment” or remove it if space is tight.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Workflow & systems design • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design”; consider merging.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it clearly from the prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g., “Built Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Rephrase technical work to show business value: “Improved communications operations through CMS enhancements, front-end implementation, analytics workflows, and cross-channel governance.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, or stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current bullets repeat themes already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role: governance, analytics, Drupal, and organization-wide communications.
- The AI search and microsite work also overlaps with “Recent Projects”; keep this entry higher-level and let the project section carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Prioritize the website transformation bullet first and make outcome clearer: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet and add performance if available: open/click rates, list growth, engagement growth, or campaign results—not just “tens of thousands.”
- Rephrase softer bullets to show business impact: “Implemented governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems that improved consistency, speed, and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate earlier NACo entries unless framed here as building the in-house studio/capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as responsibilities than outcomes. Tighten it to emphasize what changed under your leadership at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + impact: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with operational results if possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved consistency and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.” Add metrics if available (open rates, production volume, turnaround time, stakeholder teams supported).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.
- “Publishing workflows/governance” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version tactical and execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider dropping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” if messaging is not a primary differentiator versus platform/governance leadership.
- Keep wording parallel and noun-based; avoid vague terms like “planning” when “strategy” or “operations” is stronger.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Work Experience; tighten or swap for “content operations” to add specificity.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing; lead with Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-enabled search, since those are most supported by recent roles.
- Cut lower-signal or older items here (for example jQuery, possibly WordPress/SharePoint if not central to target roles) and leave detailed tool coverage to “Technical + IT.”
- Group related items for concision, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language such as “enterprise web platforms” or “large public-facing sites” rather than adding unsupported metrics here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in one place unless it is a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize business impact and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with outcome-oriented capabilities: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and SEO analysis,” “insight generation for digital decision-making”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, content and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current tool list duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive dashboarding” or “decision-support reporting.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and detailed work history. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery scope, not just tools:  
  **- Broadcast-quality video and livestream production**  
  **- In-house studio buildout and operations**  
  **- Hybrid and virtual event delivery**  
  **- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows**
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video and livestream production.”
- Consider dropping “editing” unless paired with a stronger qualifier; it undersells director-level experience.
- If space allows, add scale/context from recent work elsewhere in the CV rather than here (e.g., studio buildout, recurring advocacy programming).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in the Director/Associate roles, so this section should stay concise and differentiated.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be tightened to avoid repeating the same platform list.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, order by strength/relevance: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with Power Pages and GitHub Pages last.
- Consider adding level signals only where defensible, e.g., “Drupal (advanced)” or “Drupal (10,000+ page migration)” to make the list more credible and impact-linked.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” rather than “Power Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider merging or making this version more specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same unsupported platform list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/level to avoid sounding entry-level: **Front-end implementation for Drupal-based sites, API integrations, tag deployment, edge scripting, and deployment automation**
- Consider dropping version numbers (**HTML5/CSS3**) unless other tools also use versions; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner and more concise

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger phrasing in one place
- If **workflow automation** is covered elsewhere, avoid implying GitHub Actions overlaps with broader automation tools unless you distinguish deployment/CI use specifically

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped to reinforce senior-level systems leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and trim lower-value/general collaboration tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp”
- Remove Slack, Teams unless this section is meant to include everyday collaboration platforms; they dilute the technical signal.
- If accurate, add scope via wording in a different section rather than here, e.g., “workflow design, cross-platform automation, editorial planning systems” to show application, not just tools.
- Order by strongest/recently relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing nearby.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership already shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member communications, not just tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and order by strongest/recent relevance: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add light context to show level of use: **Enterprise email campaign operations, newsletter distribution, audience segmentation and member engagement**
- If space allows, make platform names cleaner/more current: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add a distinct capability angle (e.g., segmentation, automation, lifecycle campaigns).
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than strategic.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify outputs so it reads as the foundation for later leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add measurable outputs if available: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency of video series, website refresh scale, channel growth, or team size supported.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce broad lists: “Improved workflows across web, email, social and video; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestream and weekly advocacy video content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored/trained a digital media associate” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim broad phrases that are better demonstrated in more recent positions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Add the standout differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: replace “Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with something more specific, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, projects supported, stakeholders served, or audience/download growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership in multimedia here if later entries show the fuller progression into video and digital team leadership.
